story.sq06.title: The Orchard That Needed Heat
story.sq06.summary: Read an orchard keeper’s failed experiment and distinguish useful warmth from an unsafe closed vent.
story.sq06.s1.objective: Read the orchard trial card beside the scorched planter and examine both branch marks.
story.sq06.s1.journal: One branch burned during a sealed release; the other froze after every vent was closed. “Less fire” alone is not a solution. The old trial recorded a safe pulse and a cooling gap.
story.sq06.s1.lan: People see that black branch and want to smother every ember. The white branch died in the cold. Wen kept both so the next keeper would have to look twice.
story.sq06.s1.apprentice: The tree needed warmth and a way to let it pass. Which mark belongs to the open vent?
story.sq06.s1.note: Wen’s trial card, three winters earlier: “Closed pipe, long pulse: burned bark. No pulse, blocked vent: frost split. Open outlet, short pulse, two cooling counts: new buds. I wrote ‘fire ruined the tree’ before I checked the pipe. Crossed out now. Leave my first sentence visible so someone knows what changed my mind.”
story.sq06.s2.objective: Open the outlet, select the short pulse, and wait two marked cooling counts before choosing a fitting.
story.sq06.s2.journal: The manual handles can reproduce the trial without using a Fire technique. After the test, an insulated sleeve protects the service handle; a wide guard keeps loose ash out of the outlet. The outlet stays open with either fitting.
story.sq06.s2.lan: A sleeve makes the handle safer to touch. A guard means cleaning the outlet less often. Neither gives us permission to leave it unchecked.
story.sq06.s2.clue: Follow the trial card: outlet open → short pulse → cooling marker one → cooling marker two. If the red heat mark appears, the handle returns to neutral and the same sequence can be tried again. A failed test cannot burn a surviving tree; this planter is an empty calibration bed.
story.sq06.s2.reply_a: The sleeve is seated. I will leave the outlet mark visible so no one mistakes insulation for a closed valve.
story.sq06.s2.reply_b: The guard is seated with a cleaning gap. Ash has somewhere to fall; heat still has somewhere to go.
story.sq06.s3.objective: Post the tested pulse sequence and the chosen fitting’s maintenance note.
story.sq06.s3.journal: The posted sequence adds a readable vent-pulse preview to this room’s training record. It does not weaken a main boss or turn Fire into an enemy element. Wen’s crossed-out claim remains beside the measured result.
story.sq06.s3.lan: She wanted the mistake kept, not worshipped. Put the successful sequence beneath it, with today’s test date.
story.sq06.s3.apprentice: The note should show the outlet first. Otherwise someone might copy only the heat setting.
story.sq06.s3.record: Calibration result: outlet opened before heating; one short pulse followed by two cooling counts; no red mark. Selected fitting installed with outlet visible and accessible. Recheck after ashfall. Wen’s original and corrected observations are retained together. This result applies to this room, not to every hearth in the valley.
story.sq06.s3.retry: The open-outlet test has not completed. Reset the manual handle and follow the four visible marks; no elemental technique is required.
story.sq06.s3.done: Calibration filed. The local pulse preview is available in the training record and can be turned off.
story.sq06.epilogue.open: One season later, the reopened orchard has a few new shoots. The keeper logs their failures as carefully as their growth; the temporary regulator receives those ordinary reports.
story.sq06.epilogue.seal: The mountain orchard is retired with the intake. Wen’s trial card travels to a smaller garden beside the alternative channel, where its local settings are tested anew rather than copied blindly.
story.sq06.epilogue.shared: The maintenance network adds an outlet check before each heat pulse. The new shoots do not prove the system perfect; a failed bed still has a place in the ledger.
